sources.title: Existing Large Language Model Unlearning Evaluations Are Inconclusive
sources.what_it_covers: Information injection (finetuning + input-space attacks), spurious generalization inside TOFU, and task/format dependence: letter vs text vs greedy-generate criteria can reverse the conclusion. Recommends disclosing an injection budget, reporting a cross-format leakage matrix, and treating memorization detectors as a one-sided yardstick.
sources.what_it_does_not_cover: No formalization of censoring/truncation bias, no coverage metric, no conditional leak rate P(leak | generation state), no stratification by answer-reached / censored / collapsed / question-echo, and no discussion of decode-length limits. Stratification it proposes is by task format, not by generation state.
sources.relation_to_this_project: Closest prior work and the strongest motivation for I01. It proves evaluation conclusions are format-fragile but stops at diagnosis and recommendation; it does not give a stratified estimator, which is exactly the gap I01 fills.

sources.title: Leak@k: Unlearning Does Not Make LLMs Forget Under Probabilistic Decoding (ICML 2026)
sources.what_it_covers: Single-generation greedy evaluation creates an 'illusion of forgetting'; defines leak@k over k independent generations and proposes RULE.
sources.what_it_does_not_cover: Its axis is sampling multiplicity, not token-budget truncation or answer reachability; it does not stratify by generation state or publish a censoring interval.
sources.relation_to_this_project: Strong adjacency to I02 (budget) and I08 (decoding-path invariance). It already establishes that decoding choice moves leakage, so an uncontrolled cross-strategy gamma claim is no longer novel on its own.

sources.title: Auditing Reasoning-Trace Memorization Claims after Unlearning with Head-Conditioned Canaries
sources.what_it_covers: Defines thk_leak as substring containment of the answer inside the reasoning trace and a 'bypass gap' Delta = thk_leak - out_acc, i.e. a per-sample trace-vs-answer channel contrast, and audits whether that gap proves weight-level memorization.
sources.what_it_does_not_cover: Does not condition on answer reachability or censoring, does not stratify across systems, and does not treat collapsed / question-echo generations as separate estimands.
sources.relation_to_this_project: OVERLAPS I03 (cot-vs-answer channel split) at the metric level. I03 must not be presented as a new channel decomposition.

sources.title: K-Bench: A Benchmark for LLM Unlearning in Agentic Deployments
sources.what_it_covers: Scores leakage across six agent channels including CoT, tool calls and observations; argues final-answer-only certificates do not transfer to deployment.
sources.what_it_does_not_cover: Agentic setting; no generation-state stratification of a single model's leakage.
sources.relation_to_this_project: Second overlap for I03; also a direct challenge to any claim that 'answer-level metrics are the only problem'.

sources.title: ShadowBench: unlearning deletes names, not knowledge (NeurIPS 2026 D&B)
sources.what_it_covers: Knowledge is lexically anchored: name suppression is not knowledge removal, and the model can emit the name unprompted.
sources.what_it_does_not_cover: Does not supply a local paraphrase-recovery measurement protocol paired with this project's generations.
sources.relation_to_this_project: OVERLAPS I09 (lexical anchoring / paraphrase recovery). I09's framing is already published at NeurIPS 2026; only an incremental local protocol remains.

sources.title: Generic LLM-as-judge calibration and bias literature (multiple vendor/engineering sources)
sources.verification: search-level (multiple practitioner sources, no single canonical paper)
sources.what_it_covers: Judge-vs-human agreement, position/verbosity bias, calibrate-before-trusting, measure fail recall rather than agreement.
sources.what_it_does_not_cover: No unlearning-specific denominator-bias audit against string entity match.
sources.relation_to_this_project: I05's technique (calibration against a cheaper metric) is standard; only the unlearning application is differentiated.

sources.title: The Silent Hyperparameter: Quantifying the Impact of Inference Backends on LLM Reproducibility
sources.what_it_covers: Inference backends and numeric precision materially change outputs, so reproducibility is backend-bound.
sources.what_it_does_not_cover: No audit of an unlearning detector's threshold / judge-backend / data-version contract.
sources.relation_to_this_project: Motivates I10 but does not pre-empt it: the object audited there is the inference stack, not the detector contract.

near_duplicates.title: Existing LLM Unlearning Evaluations Are Inconclusive
near_duplicates.why: diagnoses format dependence and injection, no censoring/coverage/conditional leak rate and no generation-state strata

I01.differentiator: P(leak | generation state) with coverage and a censoring interval, plus re-ranking systems on the stratified estimator. The closest work stratifies by task format, not by generation state, and explicitly does not formalize truncation bias.

near_duplicates.title: Leak@k
near_duplicates.why: sampling-multiplicity budget, not token-budget matching across decoding strategies

I02.differentiator: Matched TOKEN budget across strategies; Leak@k varies the number of samples at a fixed decode setting.

near_duplicates.title: Head-Conditioned Canaries
near_duplicates.why: already defines a per-sample substring-based trace-vs-answer bypass gap

near_duplicates.title: K-Bench
near_duplicates.why: already scores CoT and answer channels separately

I03.differentiator: None that survives: the cot-vs-answer decomposition is published.

near_duplicates.title: Existing LLM Unlearning Evaluations Are Inconclusive
near_duplicates.why: uses fixed task-specific success thresholds (a de facto censoring rule) but never identifies it as censoring, never bounds the resulting bias, and never publishes an interval

I04.differentiator: An explicit [optimistic, pessimistic] censoring interval for evaluator truncation, required alongside every point estimate.

near_duplicates.title: generic judge calibration / bias literature
near_duplicates.why: calibration against a cheaper metric and fail-recall accounting are standard practice outside unlearning

I05.differentiator: Only the unlearning-specific denominator-bias application remains, which is application-level, not a new method.

near_duplicates.title: Leak@k
near_duplicates.why: shows decoding choice changes leakage; does not use a forced short-think channel as reachability instrumentation

near_duplicates.title: Head-Conditioned Canaries
near_duplicates.why: manipulates decoder-time conditions to audit traces, but not answer-reachability control

I06.differentiator: Uses the forced/zero-think channel as an EVALUATION instrument for reachability, not as an attack.

I07.differentiator: Makes retain utility a hard GATE on a forgetting claim rather than a co-reported metric; no retrieved hit does this, though utility co-reporting is universal.

near_duplicates.title: Leak@k
near_duplicates.why: already establishes that reported forgetting depends on the decode configuration

I08.differentiator: Recomputes an existing invariance claim (gamma) under a reachability control; the target is a specific published-style claim, not a new metric.

near_duplicates.title: unlearning deletes names, not knowledge (NeurIPS 2026 D&B)
near_duplicates.why: already establishes lexical anchoring of knowledge and name-suppression failure at scale

I09.differentiator: None that survives: lexical anchoring is published at a major venue; a 400-row local paraphrase bank adds no new claim.

near_duplicates.title: The Silent Hyperparameter
near_duplicates.why: audits inference-stack reproducibility, not an unlearning detector's threshold/judge/data contract

I10.differentiator: Audits the detector CONTRACT (threshold persistence, judge backend drift, version binding) on shipped artifacts of an inference-time unlearning system.

summary.note: This is a real external search, not a catalogue-only scan. It DEMOTES two ideas (I03, I09) that the local 34-paper catalogue could not resolve, and it demotes I05 from 'method' to 'application'. D4=2 additionally requires the cross-family reviewer to sign the specific novelty claim in idea-stage/cross_review.json.
